identity.title: The Physical and Chemical Properties of the ρ Ophiuchi A Dense Core

paper_type_evidence.quote: The physical and chemical properties of the $\rho$ Ophiuchi A core were studied using 1.3 mm continuum and molecular lines such as C$^{18}$O, C$^{17}$O, CH$_3$OH and H$_2$CO observed with the Submillimeter Array (SMA).

evidence.quote: The $\rho$ Ophiuchus cloud complex at a distance of 137.3$\pm$1.2 pc (cite: Ortiz-Leon2017)

question.value: What are the physical and chemical properties (small-scale condensations, heating, CO and N2H+ depletion, kinematics) of the rho-Oph A dense core, using SMA data combined with single-dish data?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present the 1.3 mm continuum and C$^{18}$O (2–1) images obtained with the combination of the SMA and the single-dish data.

findings_qualitative.value: C18O is bright at eastern and western ridge edges, anticorrelated with continuum and N2H+; consistent with external heating

evidence.quote: This supports the picture that the $\rho$-Oph A core is heated externally from the nearby stars Oph S1 and HD147889.

claims.hypothesis: The ridge is externally heated and its interior is cold with CO depletion
claims.experiment: Combined SMA+JCMT C18O maps and abundance maps
claims.result: C18O Tb 40-50 K at edges, below 15 K in center; abundance decreases in ridge
claims.finding: External heating by Oph S1 and HD147889; interior colder than CO freeze-out

evidence.quote: In contrast, the C$^{18}$O intensity is lower than 15–20 K at the center of the ridge where the continuum emission is bright.
the masses of all the condensations exceed the Bonnor-Ebert mass, which implies those condensations are gravitationally bounded.
